correctness.rationale: The four original branch formulas give exactly n−2m shift edges and m low plus m high reflection edges on n open cells. The shift components are the 2m index residue paths; the reflection involutions r↦−1−r and r↦2n−1−r compose to translation by 2n and connect all components since gcd(m,n)=1. There are exactly 2m leaves; removing them leaves a connected 2-regular graph, a unique (n−2m)-cycle. A finite undirected irreducible graph with backtracking has period 1 iff its unique cycle is odd, otherwise 2. Detailed balance with sin weights follows from explicit trigonometric identities, and finite Markov-chain theorems give the stated stationary limits. The 2,024-case checker matches all edge support and stationary identities, with numerical limitations explicit; the infinite argument is analytic. Grid boundaries are excluded.

Older invariant sine measure for the continuum is acknowledged, with the new fiber formula proved directly by detailed balance.

originality.rationale: The same-map 2020/2022 original papers prove finite orbit/irreducibility and offer particular 7- and 8-state periodicity examples, but do not state or imply the universal unicyclic graph and denominator parity theorem. Feres 2007 gives general reversibility. Actual literature and indexed literature searches and recoverable historical claims were compared by objects, hypotheses and implication; no stronger covering assertion was found. Unindexed equivalences remain a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed source might already state a denominator-parity criterion or general unicyclic transition graph; independent historical-priority confirmation remains open.
The theorem intentionally excludes all cell-boundary starting angles, for which probabilities can vanish differently; extension to them has not been proved.
The 2022 paper studies a larger circle-position system, so its global mixing theorem should not be confused with fiberwise mixing.

value.rationale: The 2022 primary paper explicitly contrasts an aperiodic 7-state rational fiber with a 2-periodic 8-state fiber without a general arithmetic classification. The new exact graph determines all finite rational-angle orbit sizes, entire transition support and Markov periods for every reduced numerator, then yields exact stationary weights and limiting even/odd distributions. This is a natural complete dynamical classification with applicability to spectral and hitting-time investigations; it is not a routine table recomputation or a mere Markov-chain corollary, since the hard part is the global support-graph proof.
